膜.meaning: At <part>sunset</part>, a girl blows a soap bubble so big it floats up and wraps the rising <part>moon</part>. For one night the moon wears a shimmering skin, thin as cling film, wobbling in every breeze. Astronomers call it the thinnest <kanji>membrane</kanji> in the sky.
膜.on: When it pops, a splash of soapy <sound>muck</sound> rains down on her garden.

眺.meaning: A fortune teller cracks an old turtle shell to read a <part>portent</part>, and the cracks seem to say: 'Blink and you'll miss it.' So she doesn't blink. One wide <part>eye</part> stays fixed on the shell all night. At dawn the cracks spell 'joke'. She had to <kanji>stare</kanji> for nothing.
眺.on: Her tight pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker glints as she leans in closer.
眺.kun: For breakfast she eats <sound>na</sound>an with <sound>ga</sound>rlic, still gazing at the shell.

顧.meaning: A bank decides to <part>employ</part> a <part>rubber duck</part> as head of security. It floats in the lobby fountain and slowly spins round all day, so it always sees who's behind it. Thieves give up at once. Nobody is better at turning to <kanji>look back</kanji>.
顧.on: Its deputy is a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala who watches the door.
顧.kun: In the fountain with it float a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a plastic <sound>e</sound>gg and a chunk of coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

陶.meaning: A toddler keeps her toys in an old <part>tin can</part>. Her grandmother, a potter, secretly coats it in clay, folds a damp cloth <part>wrap</part> round it to dry, then fires it in the kiln. Out comes a glazed jar with a tiny <part>pennant</part> painted on the lid. Even the toy box is <kanji>pottery</kanji> now.
陶.on: The toddler taps it with one bare <sound>toe</sound>, and it rings like a bell.
陶.kun: Inside she finds a <sound>su</sound>shi roll and a painted <sound>e</sound>gg.

肢.meaning: A wooden puppet has lost an arm. The puppeteer climbs a tree by the light of the <part>moon</part>, snaps off a thin <part>branch</part> with twigs for fingers and screws it on. The puppet waves it and tickles the cat. One new <kanji>limb</kanji>, fresh from the tree.
肢.on: The puppet celebrates by waving a tiny wooden <sound>shi</sound>eld.

漏.meaning: A proud king sleeps under his royal <part>flag</part> instead of a roof. When the <part>rain</part> starts, <part>water drops</part> seep through the stitched lion and fall, plip, plip, into the royal ear. By dawn he's floating on his mattress. Every flag has a <kanji>leak</kanji>.
漏.on: He drifts out of the door clutching a red <sound>ro</sound>se.
漏.kun: The servants run in with a <sound>mo</sound>p, and a soggy <sound>roo</sound>k shakes itself dry on the bedpost.

敢.meaning: A tiny mouse climbs the high <part>diving board</part> at the pool, holding a paper <part>fan</part> as a parachute. Everyone covers one <part>ear</part> and squints. It jumps, flutters and lands right on the lifeguard's whistle. Nobody has ever seen anything so <kanji>daring</kanji>.
敢.on: The lifeguard pins a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to its tiny chest.
敢.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the crowd, and the mouse is fed boiled <sound>e</sound>gg in a little <sound>te</sound>nt by the pool.
